content.text:
I fixed this in `@babel/generator`. The arrow function becomes `function () {...}` after transformation, and Babel was printing it without the wrapping parentheses. A statement that starts with a bare `function () {` is invalid JavaScript, hence the Node error.

**Cause:** the code that decides whether a statement-leading expression needs parentheses looks up through the surrounding expressions. It already handled member access, calls and assignments, but not postfix `++`/`--`. So in `(function () {...})().map(c, v0).map++`, the trailing `++` hid the fact that the function sits at the start of the statement.

**Fix:** in `isFirstInContext` in `packages/babel-generator/src/node/parentheses.ts`, I added postfix update expressions (`!parent.prefix`) to the cases it looks through. Prefix `++x` is left out because the operator comes first, so nothing inside it can start the statement.

**Verified:** I rebuilt the packages and generated code from an AST with a function expression inside a postfix update. The output is now `(function () {})().map++;`. Object literals and classes in the same position (`({}).x++`, `(class {}).x--`) also come out with parentheses. The existing generator test suite passes (532 passed, 4 skipped). I didn't run the full issue example through `preset-env` and the CLI, and I didn't add a new test fixture.
